# Lane I — local timing of `./mvnw -B -T1C verify`

Ran with the eight service JVMs stopped, Docker Desktop up, compose containers
(`ledgerflow-postgres`, `ledgerflow-redis`, `ledgerflow-redpanda`, `ledgerflow-lgtm`)
left running — Testcontainers spins up its own instances per module, doesn't
touch those.

## Result: BUILD FAILURE

Two modules failed, both on the same root cause:

- **ledger-service** — `HoldCommandsIT` (2 tests, both errored)
- **risk-service** — `RiskFlowIT` (2 tests, both errored)

First error line (identical shape in both):

```
java.lang.IllegalStateException: Failed to load ApplicationContext for [WebMergedContextConfiguration@...]
Caused by: ... Error creating bean with name 'postgres' defined in class path resource
  [io/ledgerflow/<service>/TestcontainersConfiguration.class]: Container startup failed
  for image redpandadata/redpanda:v25.2.1
Caused by: org.testcontainers.containers.ContainerLaunchException: Timed out waiting for
  log output matching '.*Successfully started Redpanda!.*'
Caused by: java.lang.IllegalStateException: Wait strategy failed. Container exited with code 139
```

Not a code bug — the redpanda Testcontainers image segfaulted (exit 139) on
startup. -T1C runs ledger-service and risk-service's test phases concurrently,
each spinning up its own Redpanda container alongside the compose one already
running; looks like resource contention on this machine, not a logic error.
Did not touch the code — out of scope for this box.

## Timing

Slowest three modules (Reactor Summary, wall time per module):

| module | time | result |
|---|---|---|
| ledger-service | 1:19 min | FAILURE |
| risk-service | 1:17 min | FAILURE |
| notification-service | 34.9 s | SUCCESS |

Total wall time (`time ./mvnw -B -T1C verify`): **1m23s**.

Well under the ten-minute mark, so no candidates to move behind a Maven
profile for that reason. Worth flagging anyway: ledger-service and
risk-service are exactly the two modules whose ITs bring up a Redpanda
container, and they're the two that failed — under -T1C they raced each other
(and the standing compose Redpanda) for whatever crashed the container.
CI runs single-JVM-per-module the same way but on a clean runner with no
compose stack competing for resources, so this may not reproduce there.
